HCBCOGN312.name: Psycholinguistics

Modern research draws on cognitive psychology, neuroscience, and computer science to investigate how language is processed. The course focuses primarily, though not exclusively, on the neuroscience of language. Students examine theoretical and experimental issues in speech production and comprehension, language impairments, the relationship between thought and language, and the evolution and acquisition of language. They also gain hands-on experience with experimental approaches to the study of language and develop an understanding of human linguistic capacity as a subject of multidisciplinary research. Topics covered: What is language? Evolutionary aspects of language and animal communication; language and thought; aphasia; language acquisition; bilingualism; speech comprehension; semantics; reading and dyslexia; speech production.

analysis: The closest response integrates programming, SQL databases, data visualization, machine learning and AI with statistics, social inquiry, digital strategy, rights and ethics. The added description-only Database Management Systems course teaches relational theory and SQL and is a stronger partner for the external databases course than networking. Human Rights: Law and Philosophy supplies general rights theory and protections, while the Groningen rights sequence applies them specifically to digital contexts. Sociology, ethics and governance are complementary across separate courses. Market Research and Strategy and Digital Transformation apply evidence and business decisions in settings distinct from the main technical sequence. The cognitive direction is independently supported by Groningen’s formal Cognitive Technology route with speech technology, computer vision and natural language processing. UCR links neurobiology, perception, higher-order cognition and language with algorithms, computer vision, statistics and behavior research. This provides a substantive technical and cognitive bridge without implying a separate speech engineering or human–machine interaction design sequence. Introductory Brain and Behavior precedes the available first-year Psycholinguistics offering. Later programming and data foundations support advanced image processing and deep learning. Both UCR plans differ substantively and exceed the four-course floor. The business-data and data-communication interests have curricular coverage inside the closest option and do not establish an additional distinct stable direction. The revised rows keep separate Groningen’s field project, thesis, dedicated AI regulation and human–machine interaction. Ten rows pair actual common subject matter or methods, including neural networks and research design.
